quote.text: Remember to act always as if you were at a symposium. When the food or drink comes around, reach out and take some politely; if it passes you by don't try pulling it back. And if it has not reached you yet, don't let your desire run ahead of you, be patient until your turn comes. Adopt a similar attitude with regard to children, wife, wealth and status, and in time, you will be entitled to dine with the gods. Go further and decline these goods even when they are on offer and you will have a share in the gods' power as well as their company. That is how Diogenes, Heraclitus and philosophers like them came to be called, and considered, divine.
quote.author: Epictetus
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood:
    • Just as one waits patiently for one's turn at the symposium, a parent must learn to nurture a child's growth with patience—accepting each stage of development without forcing the next.
    • Offer guidance and care with the measured grace of a host who shares his table, trusting that genuine understanding and virtue will eventually be cultivated in the young.
  • Leadership:
    • Embrace leadership with the same balance of restraint and gracious acceptance seen at a tasteful symposium—take opportunities calmly and impartially, without letting ambition cloud judgment.
    • Lead by example, knowing that by exercising self-control and patience, you inspire others to act with virtue and dignity, thus elevating the spirit of the collective.
  • Product Management:
    • Approach product development with the hospitality of a seasoned host: patiently gather input, assess feedback as it comes, and avoid rushing ahead before the right moment arises.
    • Understand that the best innovations, like the finest courses at a symposium, are those that are introduced with proper timing and care, allowing quality and resilience to flourish over haste.
